text:
alex: Hey — canary traffic started falling back to polling after proxies emitted FALLBACK_THROTTLE. Console shows route_split ~0.5 but polling lane requests and billing jumped. Anyone seen this?
maria: Saw duplicate token billing on resumed sessions. Client resumes + new polling consumers = double charge.
ben: Do we have concrete fallback logs? I only see generic 503s at edge.
alex: Payload example in edge logs: {"event":"fallback","reason":"FALLBACK_THROTTLE","route_split":0.47,"session_id":"abc123"}
jamie: Routing emits FALLBACK_THROTTLE when per-route backlog >80% for >5s. Console aggregates route_split but doesn't surface fallback_reason so ops can't correlate.
maria: Polling fallback TTL is 30s and clients don't honor resume idempotency, so retries create fresh billing streams. We should propagate an X-Resume-Idempotency header or extend TTL.
ben: Short term: add sse.fallback_reason metric tagged by route_id/proxy_zone/rollout. Also add boolean migrated_to_polling in route_split logs.
jamie: Hotfix idea: for canary, set sticky-route=true for 60s when FALLBACK_THROTTLE triggers to avoid dup consumers. Gate by rollout flag.
maria: +1. I'll open client PR to respect X-Resume-Idempotency and bump polling TTL behind canary.
ops-bot: [auto] Incident watch created: duplicate-billing alert if count >3 in 10m.
alex: Action items listed in thread. We'll monitor 48h and revert if spikes persist.
